title: 🗄️ Database Management Systems (DBMS) & SQL
description: Interview revision cheat sheet for DBMS, SQL, database design, queries, joins, transactions, indexing, normalization, and common interview questions.

sections.title: PART 1: DBMS FUNDAMENTALS
sections.description: Basic database concepts needed for software engineering interviews.

topics.title: Database & DBMS
topics.explanation:
A Database is an organized collection of data. Example: users, products, orders, and payments.

A Database Management System (DBMS) is software that stores, manages, updates, and retrieves data.

Examples of DBMS: MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Oracle.

Easy Memory:
Database = The Data
DBMS = The Software That Manages Data
topics.tldr: Database stores data. DBMS manages the data.

questions.question: Is MySQL a database or a DBMS?
questions.answer: MySQL is a DBMS. It is software used to create and manage databases.

traps.explanation: MySQL is a Database Management System that manages databases.

topics.title: Types of Databases
topics.explanation:
The two main types are:

1. Relational Database: Stores data in tables and supports relationships. Examples: MySQL and PostgreSQL.

2. Non-Relational Database: Uses flexible data models such as documents, key-value pairs, graphs, or column families.

For interviews, understand why an application may choose SQL or NoSQL.

topics.title: SQL vs NoSQL
topics.explanation:
SQL databases are relational databases. They store data in tables with rows and columns. They support relationships and JOIN operations.

NoSQL databases use flexible data models. They can be useful when the data structure changes often or when a document-based model fits the application.

Use SQL when you need strong relationships, complex queries, transactions, and structured data.

Use NoSQL when you need a flexible data model and the data naturally fits a non-relational structure.

Important: SQL and NoSQL are not competitors where one is always better. The choice depends on the application.
topics.tldr: SQL is good for structured relational data. NoSQL is useful for flexible data models.

questions.question: What is the main difference between SQL and NoSQL?
questions.answer: SQL databases use relational tables and relationships. NoSQL databases use flexible non-relational data models.

questions.question: Is NoSQL always better for large applications?
questions.answer: No. Both SQL and NoSQL can scale. The choice depends on the data model, queries, relationships, and system needs.

traps.statement: NoSQL is always better for large applications.
traps.explanation: Wrong. Both SQL and NoSQL can support large systems.

sections.title: PART 3: KEYS, RELATIONSHIPS & CONSTRAINTS
sections.description: Primary keys, foreign keys, relationships, and database rules.

topics.title: Tables, Rows, Columns & Keys
topics.explanation:
Table = Collection of related data.
Row = One record.
Column = One attribute.

Primary Key: Uniquely identifies each row.
Foreign Key: Creates a relationship with another table.
topics.tldr: Primary Key identifies a row. Foreign Key connects tables.

codeSnippets.explanation: The id column is the Primary Key.

questions.question: What is a Primary Key?
questions.answer: A Primary Key uniquely identifies each row in a table. It must be unique and cannot be NULL.

questions.question: What is a Foreign Key?
questions.answer: A Foreign Key references a key in another table to create a relationship.

topics.title: Database Relationships
topics.explanation:
One-to-One: One user has one profile.

One-to-Many: One user has many orders.

Many-to-Many: Many students can join many courses. This usually needs a junction table.
topics.tldr: Main relationships are One-to-One, One-to-Many, and Many-to-Many.

questions.question: How do you create a Many-to-Many relationship?
questions.answer: Usually by creating a junction table with foreign keys from both tables.

topics.title: Database Constraints
topics.explanation:
Constraints are rules that protect data quality.

PRIMARY KEY: Unique and NOT NULL.
FOREIGN KEY: Maintains relationships.
UNIQUE: Prevents duplicate values.
NOT NULL: Requires a value.
CHECK: Validates a condition.
DEFAULT: Provides a default value.

codeSnippets.code:
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  email VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE,
  name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  age INT CHECK (age >= 18),
  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active'
);

questions.question: What is the difference between Primary Key and UNIQUE?
questions.answer: Both prevent duplicates. A Primary Key uniquely identifies a row and cannot be NULL.

sections.title: PART 4: CRUD & SQL COMMANDS
sections.description: Basic SQL commands used in applications and interviews.

topics.title: CRUD Operations
topics.explanation:
CRUD means Create, Read, Update, and Delete.

INSERT creates data.
SELECT reads data.
UPDATE changes data.
DELETE removes data.

traps.statement: UPDATE and DELETE are safe without WHERE.
traps.explanation: Without WHERE, all matching rows can be changed or deleted.

topics.title: DELETE vs TRUNCATE vs DROP
topics.explanation:
DELETE removes rows and can use WHERE.

TRUNCATE removes all rows from a table.

DROP removes the table itself.
topics.tldr: DELETE = Remove rows. TRUNCATE = Remove all rows. DROP = Remove table.

questions.question: What is the difference between DELETE, TRUNCATE, and DROP?
questions.answer: DELETE removes rows. TRUNCATE removes all rows. DROP removes the table.

sections.title: PART 5: FILTERING, SORTING & NULL
sections.description: WHERE, operators, sorting, and NULL handling.

topics.title: WHERE & Filtering
topics.explanation:
WHERE filters rows.

Common operators:
= Equal
> Greater than
< Less than
>= Greater than or equal
<= Less than or equal
<> Not equal

Other useful keywords:
AND
OR
IN
BETWEEN
LIKE

codeSnippets.explanation: Filters users by age and city.

topics.title: ORDER BY & LIMIT
topics.explanation:
ORDER BY sorts query results.
ASC means ascending.
DESC means descending.

LIMIT restricts the number of returned rows.

codeSnippets.explanation: Returns the first 10 users sorted by age.

topics.title: NULL Values
topics.explanation:
NULL means the value is missing or unknown.

NULL is not zero.
NULL is not an empty string.

Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL to check NULL values.
topics.tldr: NULL means missing or unknown data.

codeSnippets.code:
SELECT * FROM users
WHERE phone IS NULL;
codeSnippets.explanation: Finds users with no phone value.

questions.question: Is NULL the same as zero or an empty string?
questions.answer: No. NULL means the value is missing or unknown.

sections.title: PART 6: AGGREGATION, GROUP BY & HAVING
sections.description: Aggregate functions and grouped query results.

topics.title: Aggregate Functions
topics.explanation:
Aggregate functions calculate values from multiple rows.

COUNT() counts rows.
SUM() adds values.
AVG() finds the average.
MAX() finds the highest value.
MIN() finds the lowest value.

codeSnippets.explanation: Counts users and calculates average age.

topics.title: GROUP BY & HAVING
topics.explanation:
GROUP BY groups rows with the same value.

HAVING filters grouped results.

WHERE filters rows before grouping.
HAVING filters groups after grouping.
topics.tldr: WHERE filters rows. HAVING filters groups.

codeSnippets.code:
SELECT city, COUNT(*)
FROM users
WHERE age >= 18
GROUP BY city
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;
codeSnippets.explanation: Filters rows, groups by city, and filters groups.

questions.question: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING?
questions.answer: WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters grouped results.

traps.statement: WHERE and HAVING are the same.
traps.explanation: WHERE filters rows. HAVING filters groups and aggregate results.

sections.title: PART 7: SQL JOINS
sections.description: Combining related data from multiple tables.

topics.title: INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN & Other JOINs
topics.explanation:
A JOIN combines related data from multiple tables.

INNER JOIN returns matching rows from both tables.

LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right table.

RIGHT JOIN returns all rows from the right table and matching rows from the left table.

FULL JOIN returns matching and unmatched rows from both tables.
topics.tldr: INNER = Matches only. LEFT = Everything on left. FULL = Everything from both.

codeSnippets.code:
SELECT users.name, orders.product
FROM users
INNER JOIN orders
ON users.id = orders.user_id;

questions.question: What is the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN?
questions.answer: INNER JOIN returns only matching rows. LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right table.

questions.question: What happens when there is no match in a LEFT JOIN?
questions.answer: The left table row is returned and the right table values are NULL.

topics.title: SELF JOIN
topics.explanation: A SELF JOIN joins a table with itself. It is useful for hierarchical data such as employee and manager relationships.

codeSnippets.code:
SELECT employee.name, manager.name
FROM employees employee
LEFT JOIN employees manager
ON employee.manager_id = manager.id;
codeSnippets.explanation: Connects each employee with a manager from the same table.

questions.question: What is a Self JOIN?
questions.answer: A Self JOIN joins a table with itself. It is useful for hierarchical relationships.

sections.title: PART 8: SUBQUERY & CTE
sections.description: Breaking complex SQL queries into smaller logical parts.

topics.title: Subquery
topics.explanation: A Subquery is a query inside another query. It can be used in SELECT, FROM, or WHERE.

codeSnippets.explanation: Finds employees with salary above the average.

questions.question: What is a Subquery?
questions.answer: A Subquery is a SQL query inside another SQL query.

topics.title: Common Table Expression (CTE)
topics.explanation: A CTE creates a temporary named result for a query. It can make complex SQL easier to read and organize.

codeSnippets.explanation: Creates a temporary named result and queries it.

questions.question: What is a CTE?
questions.answer: A CTE is a temporary named result used inside a SQL query.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Subquery and a CTE?
questions.answer: A Subquery is written inside another query. A CTE gives a temporary result a name and can make complex queries easier to read.

sections.title: PART 9: TRANSACTIONS & ACID
sections.description: Reliable database operations and transaction properties.

topics.title: Database Transactions
topics.explanation:
A Transaction is a group of database operations treated as one unit of work.

BEGIN starts a transaction.
COMMIT saves changes.
ROLLBACK cancels changes after an error.

Example: Money should not leave one account without reaching the other account.

questions.question: What is a Transaction?
questions.answer: A Transaction is a group of database operations treated as one unit of work.

questions.question: What is the difference between COMMIT and ROLLBACK?
questions.answer: COMMIT saves changes permanently. ROLLBACK cancels transaction changes.

topics.title: ACID Properties
topics.explanation:
Atomicity: All operations succeed together or fail together.

Consistency: Data follows database rules and stays valid.

Isolation: Concurrent transactions should not incorrectly affect each other.

Durability: Committed data should survive crashes or restarts.

questions.question: What does ACID stand for?
questions.answer: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

questions.question: What is the difference between Atomicity and Durability?
questions.answer: Atomicity means all operations succeed or fail together. Durability means committed data remains saved.

topics.title: Database Index
topics.explanation:
A Database Index is a data structure that helps the database find data faster without checking every row.

Indexes can improve WHERE, JOIN, ORDER BY, and other queries.

However, indexes use extra storage and add extra work during INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE.
topics.tldr: Index makes reads faster but can make writes slower.

codeSnippets.explanation: Creates an index on the email column.

questions.question: What is an Index?
questions.answer: An Index is a data structure that helps the database find data faster.

questions.question: Why not create an Index on every column?
questions.answer: Indexes use storage and add extra work during INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE.

traps.statement: More indexes always make a database faster.
traps.explanation: Indexes improve many read operations but can slow down write operations.

topics.title: B-Tree Index
topics.explanation: A B-Tree is a balanced tree structure commonly used for database indexes. It helps search data efficiently and supports ordered and range queries.

questions.question: Why is B-Tree useful for database indexes?
questions.answer: It supports efficient searching, ordered data, and range queries.

sections.title: PART 11: NORMALIZATION
sections.description: Reducing duplicate data and improving database design.

topics.title: Normalization & Database Anomalies
topics.explanation:
Normalization organizes database data to reduce duplication and improve consistency.

Update Anomaly: The same data must be updated in many places.

Insert Anomaly: Data cannot be added without other unrelated data.

Delete Anomaly: Deleting data accidentally removes useful related data.
topics.tldr: Normalization reduces duplicate data and database anomalies.

topics.title: 1NF, 2NF & 3NF
topics.explanation:
1NF: Each field should contain atomic values.

2NF: The table must be in 1NF and should not have partial dependency.

3NF: The table must be in 2NF and should not have transitive dependency.

For most software engineering interviews, clearly understanding 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF is enough.
topics.tldr: 1NF = Atomic values. 2NF = No partial dependency. 3NF = No transitive dependency.

questions.question: What is Normalization?
questions.answer: Normalization organizes data to reduce duplication and improve consistency.

questions.question: What is the difference between 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF?
questions.answer: 1NF uses atomic values. 2NF removes partial dependency. 3NF removes transitive dependency.

topics.title: Denormalization
topics.explanation:
Denormalization intentionally adds some duplicate data to improve read performance and reduce expensive JOIN operations.

It can improve speed but may increase data duplication.

questions.question: What is Denormalization?
questions.answer: Denormalization intentionally adds some duplicate data to improve read performance.

traps.explanation: Normalization improves data organization, but highly normalized data may require more JOIN operations.

sections.title: PART 12: SQL INTERVIEW PRACTICE
sections.description: Common SQL query patterns asked in software engineering interviews.

topics.title: Common SQL Query Patterns
topics.explanation: Software engineering interviews often test SQL problem solving. Learn common query patterns instead of memorizing only syntax.

codeSnippets.code:
-- Find duplicate emails
SELECT email, COUNT(*)
FROM users
GROUP BY email
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

-- Find users without orders
SELECT users.name
FROM users
LEFT JOIN orders
ON users.id = orders.user_id
WHERE orders.id IS NULL;
codeSnippets.explanation: Uses LEFT JOIN and NULL to find unmatched users.

codeSnippets.code:
-- Find second highest salary
SELECT MAX(salary)
FROM employees
WHERE salary < (
  SELECT MAX(salary)
  FROM employees
);
codeSnippets.explanation: Uses a Subquery to find the second highest salary.

questions.question: How do you find duplicate records?
questions.answer: Usually use GROUP BY with COUNT and HAVING COUNT greater than 1.

questions.question: How do you find records without a matching record?
questions.answer: A common solution is LEFT JOIN with IS NULL.

questions.question: How do you find the second highest salary?
questions.answer: You can use a Subquery, LIMIT and OFFSET, or a window function depending on the database.

sections.title: PART 13: INTERVIEW Q&A & FLASHCARDS
sections.description: High-yield database questions for software engineering interviews.

topics.title: High-Yield Interview Questions
topics.explanation: Common database and SQL questions asked in software engineering interviews.

questions.question: Q1: What is the difference between DBMS and RDBMS?
questions.answer: A DBMS manages database data. An RDBMS stores data in related tables and supports relationships.

questions.question: Q2: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL?
questions.answer: SQL databases use relational tables. NoSQL databases use flexible non-relational data models.

questions.question: Q3: What is a Primary Key?
questions.answer: A Primary Key uniquely identifies each row and cannot be NULL.

questions.question: Q4: What is a Foreign Key?
questions.answer: A Foreign Key creates a relationship by referencing a key from another table.

questions.question: Q5: What is NULL?
questions.answer: NULL means a value is missing or unknown. It is not zero or an empty string.

questions.question: Q6: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING?
questions.answer: WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters grouped results.

questions.question: Q7: What is the difference between DELETE, TRUNCATE, and DROP?
questions.answer: DELETE removes rows. TRUNCATE removes all rows. DROP removes the table.

questions.question: Q8: What is the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN?
questions.answer: INNER JOIN returns matching rows. LEFT JOIN returns all left rows and matching right rows.

questions.question: Q9: What is a Subquery?
questions.answer: A Subquery is a query inside another SQL query.

questions.question: Q10: What is a CTE?
questions.answer: A CTE is a temporary named result used inside a SQL query.

questions.question: Q11: What is a Transaction?
questions.answer: A Transaction is a group of database operations treated as one unit.

questions.question: Q12: What does ACID stand for?
questions.answer: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

questions.question: Q13: What is an Index?
questions.answer: An Index helps the database find data faster.

questions.question: Q14: Why not index every column?
questions.answer: Indexes use storage and can slow down INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE.

questions.question: Q15: What is Normalization?
questions.answer: Normalization reduces duplicate data and improves consistency.

questions.question: Q16: What is Denormalization?
questions.answer: Denormalization adds some duplicate data to improve read performance.

questions.question: Q17: How do you implement Many-to-Many relationships?
questions.answer: Usually with a junction table containing foreign keys from both tables.

questions.question: Q18: Can SQL databases scale?
questions.answer: Yes. SQL databases can scale. The choice depends on application requirements.

flashcards.question: WHERE vs HAVING?
flashcards.answer: WHERE filters rows. HAVING filters groups.

flashcards.question: INNER vs LEFT JOIN?
flashcards.answer: INNER returns matches. LEFT returns all left rows and matches.

flashcards.question: Index?
flashcards.answer: Faster lookup with extra write overhead.

traps.explanation: NULL means missing or unknown data.

traps.statement: HAVING and WHERE do the same job.
traps.explanation: WHERE filters rows. HAVING filters grouped results.
Too many indexes can slow down write operations.
SQL databases can scale. Database choice depends on system requirements.
Normalization improves data design but may require more JOIN operations.
